correctness.rationale: Conditional on E, the reciprocal-mean event is Z<=z*(E,h); the equation in f=1/Phi has a unique threshold. With h=sqrt(1-r), recenter m=sum wE and v=sum w(E-m)^2. Taylor implicit solving yields z*=q-hm+(h²/2)(q+[q+2phi(q)/p]v)+O_p(h³(1+max|E|)^3). Gaussian-max truncation max|E|<=h^-1/2 plus its exponentially small complement justifies integrating the order-h² formula. E(m²)=sum w² and E(v)=1-sum w² give the claimed derivative; strict Mills inequality q+phi(q)/Phi(q)>0 gives sign. The degenerate one-weight case is exactly uniform; no p->0 or n->infinity interchange claimed. Independently checked the p=1/2, w=(1/2,1/2) coefficient 1/(2pi). The inspected 12-case bivariate quadrature program is only corroborative.
residual_risks: Gaussian tail truncation constants are p-specific; neither finite quadrature nor source VERIFY_OK alone proves quantifiers.

evidence: Published dependence-class calibration is for independence/negative orthant or specified copulas; heavy-tail second-order papers send p->0 at a fixed dependence model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither fixed-correlation tail asymptotics nor a Gaussian numerical conjecture dominates the all-fixed-p, r->1 analytic derivative; limit order noncommutes without extra uniform estimates.
